name: Bike repair: fixing a flat in a race
description: Road and tri bikes: tubes, tubeless, CO2, and getting back on fast.

cards.front: First thing to do when you flat during a race
cards.back: Pull safely off the course, out of the way of other riders.

cards.front: Before removing the rear wheel, shift into…
cards.back: The smallest rear cog (hardest gear), so the wheel drops out easily.

cards.front: Rim brakes: what to open before removing the wheel?
cards.back: The brake caliper's quick-release, so the tire clears the pads.

cards.front: Disc brakes: what not to do with the wheel out?
cards.back: Don't squeeze the brake lever, or the pads close together. Use a pad spacer if you have one.

cards.front: Essential race flat kit
cards.back: Spare tube, 2 tire levers, CO2 inflator + cartridge(s) or a mini pump, a tire boot, and a multitool.

cards.front: Why carry a tire boot?
cards.back: To cover a sidewall or tread cut so the new tube doesn't bulge out and burst.

cards.front: Emergency tire boot if you have none
cards.back: A folded dollar bill, gel wrapper, or energy-bar wrapper.

cards.front: Before installing the new tube, always…
cards.back: Run your fingers carefully around the inside of the tire to find and remove whatever caused the flat.

cards.front: Why add a little air to the new tube before installing it?
cards.back: It gives the tube shape so it doesn't twist or get pinched under the tire bead.

cards.front: Seating the bead: where do you start, and where do you finish?
cards.back: Start at the valve, work both ways around, and finish opposite it. Then push the valve up into the tire so the tube isn't trapped under the bead.

cards.front: Trick for the last, tight section of bead
cards.back: Push the already-seated bead into the rim's center channel all the way around to gain slack.

cards.front: Why avoid tire levers for the last bit of bead?
cards.back: Levers can pinch and puncture the new tube.

cards.front: After seating the tire, before full inflation, check…
cards.back: That no tube is caught under the bead and the bead line sits evenly all around.

cards.front: Presta valve: what to do before inflating?
cards.back: Unscrew the small knurled nut at the tip (and tap it to free it).

cards.front: Deep-section race wheels need what from your spare tube?
cards.back: A long enough valve stem (e.g. 60–80 mm), or a valve extender.

cards.front: Why hold a CO2 cartridge with a sleeve or gloves?
cards.back: It gets extremely cold as it discharges and can freeze-burn your fingers.

cards.front: After the race, what should you do with a CO2-filled tube?
cards.back: Let it out and refill with air. CO2 seeps through butyl tubes quickly.

cards.front: Roughly how much does one 16 g CO2 cartridge inflate?
cards.back: About one road tire to riding pressure. Carry two in case the first one gets wasted.
choices: A mountain bike tire to 100 psi

cards.front: Two parallel slits in a tube ('snakebite') mean…
cards.back: A pinch flat: the tube got pinched against the rim, usually from low pressure.

cards.front: A puncture on the inner side of the tube (rim side) usually means…
cards.back: Rim tape problem: a spoke hole or sharp edge is exposed.

cards.front: Tubeless: what fixes a hole too big for sealant?
cards.back: A tire plug (a 'bacon strip'), then re-inflate.

cards.front: Tubeless sealant hissing: how to help it seal?
cards.back: Spin the wheel so the hole is at the bottom, letting sealant pool over it, then ride a bit.

cards.front: Tubeless tire won't hold after plugging: last resort?
cards.back: Remove the valve and install a spare inner tube.

cards.front: Reinstalling the rear wheel: where should the chain go?
cards.back: Over the smallest rear cog, then drop the wheel into the dropouts.

cards.front: Quick-release skewer: correct closing technique
cards.back: Close the lever firmly enough to leave an imprint in your palm. Don't spin it like a wing nut.

cards.front: Last check before riding off after a rim-brake wheel change
cards.back: Close the brake caliper quick-release again and test both brakes.

cards.front: Chain dropped off the small chainring: fastest fix?
cards.back: Shift to the small ring, push the rear derailleur cage forward for slack, and lift the chain on by hand.

cards.front: Why line the tire logo up with the valve?
cards.back: So the hole in a tube points you to the matching spot on the tire to search for the cause.

cards.front: Patch or replace the tube mid-race?
cards.back: Replace. It's much faster. Patch the old tube later.
choices: Use sealant in a butyl tube

cards.front: Triathlon rule on mechanical help
cards.back: Usually no outside assistance: you fix it yourself. Check your race's rules.

cards.front: Best way to get fast at flat changes
cards.back: Practice at home and time yourself, with the exact kit you race with.

cards.front: Where should spare-tube kit go on a tri bike?
cards.back: Somewhere you can reach with the bike upside down, e.g. a saddle pack or behind-seat mount, secured so it can't eject.

cards.front: Tire direction arrows: does it matter?
cards.back: Yes, on many tires. Follow the arrow for intended grip and wear.

cards.front: Rolling but rubbing after reinstalling the wheel?
cards.back: The wheel probably isn't fully seated in the dropouts. Reopen, push it fully in, then close.
